prompt: Businesses that modify work schedules to reasonably accommodate the needs of all employees are complying with the requirements of the
explanation: Americans with Disabilities Act. This act protects workers with physical and/or mental disabilities from discrimination. The law also states that businesses must make reasonable accommodations for disabled workers unless that puts an undue burden on the business. Reasonable accommodation involves making adjustments so that qualified individuals can perform the necessary job activities. For example, reasonable accommodation might include modifying work schedules so disabled employees could arrive and depart at different times if they relied on special bus service to transport them to work. There is an Equal Employment Opportunity Commission but not an Equal Employment Opportunity Act. The Civil Rights Act of 1991 expanded previous civil rights legislation by allowing employees who feel they have been the victims of discrimination to sue their employers. The Occupational Safety and Health Act stipulates that workers may not be disciplined or discharged for refusing to work in unsafe environments or because they report an alleged violation to the appropriate government agency.

prompt: In what type of business is the owner personally liable for any debts of the business?
explanation: Sole proprietorship. A sole proprietorship is a form of business ownership in which the business is owned by one person. This means that the owner is liable for the debts of the business. A corporation is owned by its stockholders who share the responsibility for debts. A hybrid is a form of business ownership that combines elements of corporations and either sole proprietorships or partnerships.

prompt: Which of the following was developed to eliminate trade barriers among three specific countries:
explanation: North American Free Trade Agreement. The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) is a trade agreement among Canada, Mexico, and the United States to lower trade barriers. The purpose is to promote and encourage free trade among these three countries. The European Union is the European trading bloc that promotes economic development and free trade among the member European nations. The North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) is an alliance of 26 North American and European countries. The Southeast Asian Group does not exist.

prompt: What should bank employees be willing to accept when defending their ideas objectively?
explanation: Critical feedback. When bank employees present their ideas to management or coworkers, they should be prepared to defend those ideas and provide supporting information. They also should be willing to accept critical feedback because others might not agree with the ideas or have different opinions. Being prepared will help employees remain objective and be able to offer logical evidence to back up their ideas. Critical feedback is often useful because it allows employees to view their ideas from a different perspective. Defending ideas usually does not involve accepting additional responsibility or nonverbal support. It is not acceptable to attack employees on a personal level because of their ideas.

prompt: A complex written report is often circulated to many employees working in finance, some of whom may not take time to read it. For this reason, the writer should
choices: write in an informal, conversational style that is easy to understand.
include a lot of graphics to reduce the number of words.
eliminate support materials, such as an appendix and a bibliography.
present a summary of the findings in the front part of the report.
explanation: Present a summary of the findings in the front part of the report. This enables persons who do not need or wish to read the whole report to learn the most important information. A complex written report is formal and should not be written in an informal style. The writer should not use more graphics than are appropriate for the content. Support materials, such as an appendix and a bibliography, are important and should be included.

prompt: "We will introduce the finance new manager, review financial reports for area B, solve problems in processing, and discuss new items." This is an example of a staff meeting's
explanation: Agenda. The agenda lists what is to be discussed during the meeting. The schedule indicates the date and time at which the meeting will take place. Materials are the supplies used in the meeting. Minutes are a report of what is said and done at a meeting, usually distributed to attendees after the meeting is over.

prompt: What is often the result of positive customer/client relations?
explanation: Repeat business. Salespeople who develop positive relationships with customers usually are able to maintain those customers over a period of time. The benefit of having positive customer relationships is repeat business. Salespeople know that it is more time consuming and expensive to attract new customers than it is to keep existing customers. Therefore, salespeople try to build good relationships with their customers in order to keep their business. Positive customer/client relations do not result in more competition, additional stress, or increased training.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a bank employee reinforcing a service orientation through communication:
choices: Offering to find information for customers
Agreeing that customers are always right
explanation: Offering to find information for customers. Bank employees often need to communicate information to customers in order to provide service. On occasion, employees may not know the answer to a customer's question, but instead of saying they do not know, they should offer to find out. Obtaining information for customers is an effective way of reinforcing a service orientation through communication. Employees should help all customers rather than be selective about who they serve. Employees should never tell customers that they are misinformed. Employees should be tactful when dealing with complaints because customers are not always right.

prompt: In order for something to be defined as an economic good, it must be capable of
explanation: Satisfying wants and needs. An economic good is also a physical object that is useful, scarce, and transferable. Cost, popularity, and durability influence the item's price.

prompt: Which of the following groups of words best describes wants:
explanation: Unlimited, changing, and competing. Wants are considered unlimited because people always have them. People's desires change with different situations or circumstances. Wants are considered competing because people must choose which wants to satisfy at any one time. Compensating does not describe wants.

prompt: What factor affects a product's utility to the individual customer?
explanation: Consumer's age. Basic demand for a product is not determined by its price but by its utility, or usefulness. How useful products are perceived to be is based upon such things as the consumer's age, gender, occupation, education, and income. None of the other alternatives has a bearing on product utility.

prompt: For a business, income remaining after payment of expenses is
explanation: Profit. The monetary reward business owners receive for taking the risks involved in investing in a business is profit. Losses result when expenses are greater than income. Capital is the assets of a business. Debt is the amount of money owed to someone else.

prompt: If monopolies are illegal in the United States, why are some utility companies allowed to exist as monopolies?
choices: The government doesn't know they exist.
The companies are regulated by government.
explanation: The companies are regulated by government. Although monopolies generally are considered illegal in the United States, the government allows some monopolies to exist under controlled conditions. This happens when legislators feel that one large company can more efficiently serve consumers than several small ones. For example, many utility companies are regulated monopolies and operate under close state and federal supervision. The government knows the companies exist, yet it does not own them. Indirect competitors are business rivals which offer dissimilar goods or services.

prompt: A business employee is assigned to handle all incoming phone orders. This specific assignment is considered to be specialization by
explanation: Task. Specialization by task allows the worker to become highly skilled in one, very small portion of a job. Specialization by trade/profession is the type of work which you perform in order to earn a living. Specialization by stage of production occurs when more than one stage is required to change a raw material into a finished product.

prompt: Which of the following is a barrier that affects economies of scale:
explanation: Input price increases. Economies of scale are a condition that occurs when a business's input increases by a certain percentage (e.g., 50%), which results in a larger percentage increase of output (e.g., 100%), causing the cost of each unit that is produced to decrease. A barrier to economies of scale occurs when the cost of the resources that the business needs to produce the goods increases. When resource costs increase, the cost to produce each unit also increases. Fewer competitors, accounting practices, and pricing strategies do not directly affect a business's actual production activities in relation to the economies of scale.

prompt: Which of the following is a type of unemployment that often creates serious economic problems in a country:
explanation: Cyclical. Cyclical unemployment occurs when spending decreases and a country is heading into a recession. This is a serious economic problem because many people are out of work, which means that consumer spending will continue to decline. The more spending decreases, the more workers become unemployed because production also decreases. If countries are not able to stop the cycle, it often leads to a depression. Structural unemployment occurs when the types of jobs change and employees need new skills. Frictional unemployment occurs when workers are between jobs or changing jobs. Seasonal unemployment occurs when jobs change due to the time of year.

prompt: What is the resulting condition when countries depend upon each other for products they cannot produce alone?
explanation: Economic interdependence. Countries are interdependent because they need imports essential to the welfare of their citizens, and they need exports to provide opportunities for employment. A comparative advantage results when one country has an advantage over others in the production of a good or service. When exports exceed imports, a country experiences a trade surplus; when imports are greater than exports, a country experiences a trade deficit.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a cultural and social characteristic that would have an impact on financial institutions that do business with certain foreign countries:
explanation: Role of women. The role of women in a country often has an impact on financial institutions doing business with that country. In some countries, women have very few opportunities to work and do not participate in business activities. Therefore, many businessmen in these countries are not accustomed to working with women. In other societies, women have equal opportunities and participate in business on the same level with men. Financial institutions need to be aware of the role of women in other countries in order to avoid creating problems or offending their customers. The source of income, type of climate, and variety of industry are not social and cultural characteristics of foreign countries.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a situation in which businesses use persuasion:
explanation: Sales presentation. Businesses use persuasion in a variety of sales situations, including sales presentations and letters. The purpose of a sales presentation is to persuade a customer or potential customer to buy the business's goods or services. To do this effectively, the business identifies the customer's needs and uses techniques to appeal to those needs. For example, an effective sales presentation might identify a specific problem and persuade the customer that the business has the best solution to the problem. A job application and an interview session are situations in which employees or potential employees use persuasion. Classroom instruction is intended to teach rather than persuade.

prompt: Which of the following is a common cause of stress in certain employees who work in financial analysis:
explanation: Personality. Personality is an individual's qualities or traits and behavior. Some employees often experience more stress because of their personalities. For example, employees who are extremely competitive and strive for perfection all the time may experience more stress than employees who are more easygoing and relaxed. If employees realize that their personalities are causing them stress, they may be able take measures to control the stress. Headaches and anxiety are often symptoms of stress. Severe and constant stress might lead to burnout.

prompt: When planning to make your vision a reality, you must first consider
choices: the resources that you will need.
the wording of your mission statement.
explanation: The resources that you will need. Vision is the future you desire to create and involves making positive changes to make it happen, which requires determination and hard work. A vision for the future begins with a general or broad view of a desired outcome, such as helping sick children or ending world hunger. Once you determine your vision, you must figure out what resources you will need to carry out the vision, such as money (financial considerations), training (education and skills), and volunteers (human resources). Personal financial goals may not affect how you carry out your vision. Volunteers give their time freely, so they are not hired (paid) employees. A mission statement is a brief summary of what a business owner wants a business to be doing. Mission statements often change over time, but vision statements remain the same.

prompt: When employees demonstrate adaptability, they are able to be
explanation: Flexible. Flexibility is the ability to adapt to changes as they occur. When employees are demonstrating adaptability, they are able to be flexible and adjust to changing conditions. When employees demonstrate adaptability, they are not necessarily being aggressive, honest, or creative.

prompt: Authoritarian managers prefer to exercise __________ control over employees.
explanation: A high degree of. Authoritarian managers prefer to exercise a high degree of control over employees. They tend to see themselves as the sole source of authority and to supervise the people under them very closely. They usually provide highly specific plans, procedures, and instructions for employees to follow.

prompt: The number-one reason why people lose their jobs is that they
explanation: Can't get along with others. These people are fired because they cause more difficulty for a business than those who don't understand their work, take too much time off, or fail to follow directions. These problems can be corrected.

prompt: Which of the following often is an effective technique for financial planners to use while interviewing prospective clients:
explanation: Take notes. Financial planners often interview prospective clients to explain their services and determine what type of services the clients want and need. It is often useful for financial planners to take notes during the interview process in order to have accurate information about clients for future reference. For example, planners may need to know clients' retirement goals in order to develop a realistic investment plan. The purpose of interviewing usually is to ask questions and gather information. Therefore, it is not necessarily useful to use visuals, give instructions, or prepare orders.

prompt: The Fair Credit Reporting Act is important to consumers because it
choices: provides guidelines that institutions must use in extending credit.
gives them the right to inspect the files of their credit history.
ensures that they are not denied credit for any discriminatory reason.
makes it easy for them to compare the terms of different credit systems.
explanation: Gives them the right to inspect the files of their credit history. This lets the consumer make sure that there are no errors in the report or, if errors exist, to have them corrected. The Truth-in-Lending Act makes it easy for consumers to compare the terms of different credit systems and provides guidelines that institutions must use in extending credit. The Equal Credit Opportunity Act protects consumers from being discriminated against when applying for credit.

prompt: Which of the following types of insurance do businesses frequently offer as part of their employee benefit plan:
explanation: Health. Many businesses offer health insurance as part of their employee benefit plan. Some businesses pay all of the premiums for their employees' coverage while others charge their employees a portion of the expense. Health insurance often is an important part of an employee's overall compensation package. Automobile, property, and liability insurance usually are the responsibility of the individual employee.

prompt: Mr. Gates owns two successful businesses and would like to open a third. Which of the following business activities should he consider first:
explanation: Accounting. Accounting is the process of keeping financial records. Accurate accounting records can show the owner how the business is doing at any point in time, and enable the owner to plan for the future. Production creates the products that businesses offer for sale. Marketing provides the avenue for businesses to sell their products and consumers a way to obtain needed products. Management oversees all of the other business activities.

prompt: A business estimates that its cash flow from sales during the coming season will be higher than for the same period last year, based on last year's financial information and
explanation: Industry trends. An industry trend is the direction in which a particular industry is moving. The combination of financial information with industry trends helps businesses to estimate the amount of cash flow necessary to continue operations and increase profits. If industry trends indicate that conditions are favorable for sales to remain strong, then a business might estimate that its cash flow from sales will increase. Future earnings and potential costs are what a business is predicting with the help of information about industry trends. Businesses use all available information in an effort to set realistic goals.

prompt: Calculate a business's cash flow if it has cash receipts of $345,675, operating expenses of $312,480, and taxes of $7,500.
explanation: $33,195. Cash flow is the movement of funds into and out of a business and determines the amount of cash the business has to work with at any given time. Cash flow is calculated by subtracting the amount of cash going out of the business (expenses) from the amount coming into the business (receipts). In this example, subtract the operating expenses from the cash receipts ($345,675 - $312,480 = $33,195). The taxes are included in the operating expenses and not subtracted separately.

prompt: If an invoice lists terms of 4/10, net 30 on a net amount of $3,675.50, calculate the total if the customer takes the discount.
explanation: $3,528.48. Invoices list the terms that indicate when payment is expected. The terms are often expressed as discounts that are available if the customer pays within a certain amount of time. In this example, the customer may take a 4% discount if the invoice is paid within 10 days of the invoice date. To calculate the discount, multiply the net amount by 4% ($3,675.50 x 4% or .04 = $147.02). Subtract this figure from the net amount to calculate the total after discount ($3,675.50 - $147.02 = $3,528.48).

prompt: An operating budget projects not only the amount of operating expenses for a certain period of time but also the expected amount of
explanation: Revenue. Operating budgets are concerned with a business's expenses and revenue. The operating budget projects the amount of money needed to operate the business over a certain period of time. It also estimates the amount of revenue expected to be generated during the same period. The expected revenue should be more than the projected expenses in order to have a balanced operating budget. The operating budget does not project turnover in employees, charges for goods or services, or taxes.

prompt: Calculate a business's profitability ratio if its net profit is $125,000 and its net sales are $775,000.
explanation: 16%. Businesses often calculate profitability based on the relationship between net profit and net sales in order to determine if they are earning an acceptable return on their investment. One formula for calculating the profitability ratio is net profit divided by net sales ($125,000 ÷ $775,000 = .161 or 16%). Businesses track this ratio from year to year in order to determine if profits are increasing or decreasing in proportion to sales. If sales increase but the profitability ratio decreases, the business knows that it is spending too much on the sales effort and may need to reduce costs or increase prices.

prompt: On which of the following would you expect to find a business's actual expenses listed by category:
explanation: Profit-and-loss statement. A profit-and-loss statement is also known as an income statement. An income statement is a summary of business transactions that shows net profit before and after taxes by analyzing sales, purchases, cost of goods sold, and operating expenses for a specified period. A balance sheet shows the financial status of the business. A cash flow projection is a budget that would include estimates of expenses. Break-even analysis is a financial analysis showing the level of sales needed to pay the operating expenses and to make debt payment.

prompt: A method used to determine whether an applicant qualifies for credit is
explanation: Credit scoring. In credit scoring, numeric values are assigned to factors that affect a person's creditworthiness. In order for a customer to be granted credit, s/he must score at an acceptable level. A credit bureau provides information that a business could use in its scrutiny of credit applicants. Aging accounts is the process of analyzing a business's past-due accounts receivable. Garnishment is the legal withholding by an employer of part of a worker's wages which are turned over to his/her creditors.

prompt: A financial manager who postpones a major capital investment, such as purchasing an upgraded computer network, is maximizing
explanation: Short-term profit. A financial manager who postpones a major capital investment is maximizing profit, which is by definition short term. Because the business is not spending money on a major purchase, it has more profit. This approach is taken at the expense of long-term wealth maximization. Short-term wealth and long-term profit are not meaningful approaches.

prompt: In order to optimize rate of return when selecting among investments, it is important to consider capital gain or loss as well as
explanation: Cash dividends. When selecting among investments in order to optimize return, investors should consider not only capital gain or loss but also any cash dividends, such as a stock dividend or rent on investment property. Optimizing rate of return does not involve the consideration of treasury note interest rates (unless one is considering investing in treasury notes), net sales, or gross domestic product.

prompt: A person who purchases a contract with an insurance company that will pay the person a sum of money for life is purchasing a(n)
explanation: Annuity. An annuity is a type of investment that earns interest. People often purchase annuities as a way of supplementing retirement plans or of investing the money they received from company pension plans. The annuity, or contract with an insurance company, can pay individuals a sum of money for life, or for a specific number of years, or as a lump sum at a designated time. Pension plans are often managed by an employee's company. A trust involves a designated individual managing the assets of another person. A mutual fund is a collection of stocks, bonds, and other investments.

prompt: By reviewing a client's previous tax returns, a financial advisor is able to determine the client's tax
explanation: History. Financial advisors often review a client's previous tax returns to understand the client's tax history in regards to income, deductions, etc. This information may be helpful in preparing future tax returns. It also may enable a financial advisor to suggest ways that the client might reduce future tax liabilities. A client's tax status might change from year to year, such as getting married and filing a joint return. Taxes are liabilities rather than benefits. Tax forms are the tax returns.

prompt: In addition to age, marital status, dependent status, and wages (including tips and other compensation), what information is necessary to complete a client's personal income tax forms?
choices: Taxable interest, deductions, and adjustments to income
Taxable interest, deductions, and the previous year's income
Deductions, adjustments to income, and the previous year's income
explanation: Taxable interest, deductions, and adjustments to income. These categories cover the basic elements required to complete a client's tax forms. It is not necessary to know the previous year's income.

prompt: When developing a client's account statement, what do businesses often use to calculate the labor charges?
explanation: Hourly billing rate. Businesses that bill clients for labor charges usually develop an hourly billing rate that covers all the costs associated with providing the labor. These costs usually include wages and salaries, benefits, operating expense, and desired profit. For example, when developing a client's account statement, the business determines the number of hours of labor and multiplies the time by the hourly billing rate. If there are 25 hours of labor and the hourly billing rate is $35, the client's statement will indicate a charge of $875. Monthly salary, overhead expense, and profit margin are factors that a business might consider when determining the hourly billing rate to charge for labor.

prompt: Which of the following assists clients in establishing financial goals:
choices: Postponing clients' questions until a later meeting
explanation: Requesting clients' financial documents. When assisting clients in establishing financial goals, it is helpful to look at their financial documents, such as earnings and investments. It is also helpful to consider clients' upcoming life changes and to answer any questions they may have. Identifying clients' pastimes might also be helpful, but evaluation is not necessary.

prompt: Financial planners who sell insurance and mutual funds often are compensated on a __________ basis.
explanation: Commission. A commission is a percentage of the total sale amount paid to the individual who makes the sale. Financial planners who sell insurance and mutual funds usually are compensated by the companies whose insurance and mutual funds they sell. The commission is often an agreed-upon percentage that compensates the financial planners for selling the financial products. Financial planners are compensated when they sell insurance and mutual funds; however, that may not be on a monthly basis. Financial planners who sell insurance and mutual funds are not compensated on a flat-rate basis or a tax-exempt basis.

prompt: Which of the following is a factor that businesses consider when determining the overall cost of raising capital by obtaining a bank loan:
explanation: Interest rates. Businesses often need to raise additional capital, or funds, to cover unexpected expenses or to make large investments. One way to raise capital is to obtain a bank loan. However, before obtaining a loan, businesses should consider the interest rates that they will be charged for the use of those funds. If the current interest rate is high and a business needs a five-year loan, the overall cost of the capital also will be high. Businesses may decide that the costs are too high and look for other ways to raise capital. Businesses usually do not pay legal fees when raising capital by obtaining a bank loan. Trade credit involves obtaining short-term credit from suppliers. Cash flow is the movement of funds into and out of a business.

prompt: In the process of verifying a company's financial statements, independent auditors examine which of the following:
explanation: Internal controls. Internal controls are the procedures and security measures set up and maintained by the company. While the enforcement of internal controls is key to the "fairness" of the financial statements-the levels of compensation, how employees are managed (human resource management), and the stock price are not. These three are not reflected on the financial statements; neither are they involved in the verification process.

prompt: A business estimating the expected return on investments, such as dividends from stocks and bonds, is evaluating future
explanation: Cash flow. Cash flow is the movement of funds into and out of a business. When evaluating future cash flow, businesses often estimate the income they might receive as a result of investments. For example, if a business receives dividends from stocks and bonds, the business has additional cash flowing into the business on a regular basis. By estimating the expected return on investments, a business can determine if it will have sufficient cash flow to cover operating expenses or expand the business. Depreciation is the reduction in value of goods occurring over a period of time. A liability is a debt. A business estimating the expected return on investments is not evaluating future sales risk.

prompt: Other than conducting a SWOT analysis, what could an individual do to determine the financial strengths or weaknesses of a business?
choices: Discuss employee satisfaction with the steering committee.
explanation: Examine the financial statements. The financial statements indicate if a business is earning a profit. Though interviewing the Director of Human Resources, reviewing the marketing plan, and discussing employee satisfaction with the steering committee may reveal some strengths or weaknesses, none are used to determine the financial strengths or weaknesses of a business.

prompt: When determining the optimal mix and type of assets to acquire, businesses consider their long-term financial needs as well as the need to
explanation: Access cash quickly. Businesses acquire a variety of assets over a period of time. These assets include equipment, property, investments in other companies, and cash. When determining the optimal mix and type of assets to acquire, businesses consider their long-term financial needs because certain investments increase in value over time and add to the net worth of the business. Businesses also consider the need to access cash quickly because some assets are easier to convert to cash than others. For example, savings accounts are assets that businesses can access quickly in order to obtain cash. Businesses want to develop the right mix of assets so they can access cash when necessary and also increase their net worth. Property is an asset. Not all businesses issue stock dividends, but if they do, dividends are expenses paid to others. Businesses do not determine the optimal mix and type of assets to acquire in order to calculate income taxes.

prompt: A business borrowing money to purchase an investment that will have more worth than what it costs to borrow the money is an example of
explanation: Leverage. Businesses often use leverage to increase their assets. This involves borrowing money to make an investment that generates more income than the interest it pays on the borrowed money. For example, a business borrows $50,000 to purchase stock in another company. The business pays back the loan with interest over a two-year period for a total of $60,000. However, at the end of two years, the stock in the other company is valued at $80,000. The business has leveraged the $50,000 loan into an $80,000 investment. If it sells the stock, the business will have additional income of $20,000 after paying the $10,000 in interest. Although the business is increasing its assets, this is not considered an example of expansion. Equity is the net worth of the business. Liquidity is the ability to convert assets to cash.

prompt: In order to accelerate cash receipts, a company might do all of the following except:
explanation: Reduce frequency of payments. Reducing the frequency of payments would decelerate cash receipts, not accelerate them. More frequent payments accelerate receipts. Other methods for accelerating cash receipts include establishing a lockbox (reduces mail float), providing return envelopes (increases customer convenience), and using pre-authorized debits (automates payment process).

prompt: Which of the following is a factor that businesses usually consider when deciding when to spend cash:
explanation: Preferred cash balance. Businesses usually establish a preferred cash balance which is the amount of cash that the business always wants to have on hand. Cash in excess of that amount is available for the business to spend. If the business estimates that it will have expenses that will cost more than the available cash, it usually decides to begin financing activities in order to borrow money and maintain the preferred cash balance. When deciding when to spend cash, businesses usually do not consider the estimated capital budget, projected interest rate, or required loan schedule.

prompt: One reason why some businesses decide to factor accounts receivable is to obtain
explanation: Needed cash. Factoring is a type of debt financing that involves selling accounts receivable for a discounted amount to another company. The factoring company buys a business's accounts receivable for less than they are worth and then collects the receivables. The business that sells its accounts receivable receives needed cash quickly rather than waiting for customers to pay their accounts. Some businesses factor accounts receivable if they are experiencing a cash-flow problem and need to obtain cash. Trade credit is another type of debt financing, but it does not involve factoring accounts receivable. Equity financing involves selling part of the ownership of a business to acquire capital. Leverage is borrowing money to acquire an asset that will have more value than the cost of borrowing the money.

prompt: Which of the following is a characteristic of marketable securities:
explanation: Short-term investments. A characteristic of marketable securities is that they are short-term investments that businesses usually intend to sell within a year. They are temporary investments that many businesses make when they have excess cash that they do not need to spend in the near future. The benefit of investing in marketable securities, such as government bonds or stock in other companies, is that the business can sell them quickly and easily to obtain cash. Marketable securities are investments rather than liabilities or debts. They are short-term investments rather than long-term assets.

prompt: When computing the cost of inventory, businesses include the cost of purchasing the items as well as the cost of
explanation: Handling and storing. The cost of inventory includes more than the cost of purchasing the items. It also includes the cost of handling and storing the items, insuring the items, paying taxes on the items, etc. When businesses compute the cost of inventory, they include all of these costs to obtain an accurate dollar figure for the costs associated with maintaining an inventory. Shipping and transporting costs are included in the cost of purchasing inventory items. The cost of inventory does not include the cost of preparing visual displays or of marking prices.

prompt: When projecting future operations, it is important for businesses also to develop projected
explanation: Financial plans. Projecting future operations involves forecasting the condition of the business in the future. This might include projecting that sales will increase by a certain percentage, or that the size of the company will double, or that the workforce will increase, etc. When projecting these operations, businesses also need to develop projected financial plans in order to be prepared to fund the operations. If the size of the company will double, then there will be additional expenses to pay. The business must plan to pay those expenses. When projecting future operations, businesses do not develop projected tax schedules, stock options, or inventory methods.

prompt: One reason why it is important for businesses to manage the cash-flow cycle is to make sure funds are available to
explanation: Pay operating expenses. Businesses monitor cash flow in order to make sure there are sufficient funds coming into the business to pay expenses, such as operating costs. Many businesses know the approximate amount of expenses they need to pay each month. Therefore, they may set up payment schedules to coincide with cash flowing into the business. Also, they may offer discounts to customers to encourage them to pay earlier in order to increase cash flow. The goal is to maintain a positive cash flow to cover expenses. Businesses may make investments, declare dividends, or award employee bonuses if the business shows a sufficient amount of profit. However, these activities are not necessarily tied to cash flow.

prompt: A business comparing standard costs with actual costs is an example of
explanation: Analyzing variances. Standard costs are those costs that should be incurred if activities take place under normal circumstances. Businesses use standard costs as a benchmark when comparing costs to determine if actual costs varied from the standard. This process is known as analyzing variances. For example, if actual costs are higher than standard costs, a variance exists. This might indicate a problem that the business should identify and correct in order to bring actual costs in line with standard costs. Comparing standard costs with actual costs is not an example of calculating expenses, estimating payables, or predicting returns.

prompt: By preparing quarterly reports, corporations are able to analyze
explanation: Current financial data. Corporations usually are required to prepare quarterly reports that contain current financial information. By preparing quarterly reports, corporations are able to analyze the current financial condition of the business and make adjustments if needed. Also, this information tells stockholders if their investment is growing in value or if it is time to sell. Corporations analyze current financial data when preparing quarterly reports rather than investment options, collection procedures, or inventory systems.

prompt: One important similarity between horizontal and vertical financial data analyses is the comparison of figures
explanation: Within the same category. Both horizontal and vertical financial data analyses compare figures within the same category. Ratio analysis is used to compare figures from different categories. Horizontal financial analysis typically compares one or more years' worth of data. Vertical financial analysis can compare data within one fiscal year.

prompt: If McDonald's Corp. has 1.26 billion shares of common stock outstanding and its stock price is currently $33.58, what is the value of its common stock?
explanation: $42.31 billion. The value of a company's common stock, called market capitalization, is calculated by multiplying the number of common shares outstanding by the current stock price. In this case, the calculation is 1.26 billion shares x $33.58, or $42.31 billion.

prompt: How much money will you have if you deposit $1,500 a year for six years into an account that pays 4%. Using a table that shows the future value of an annuity of $1, you find a value of 6.633. How much will you have at the end of six years?
explanation: $9,949.50. When determining the future value of an annuity, the amount of the annuity is multiplied by the value that corresponds to the interest rate and the number of periods on a future value of an annuity table. The value for six years at 4% is 6.633. With annual deposits of $1,500, you will have $9,949.50 at the end of six years ($1,500 x 6.633 = $9,949.50).

prompt: Diversifying investments primarily protects investors against
explanation: Market fluctuations. By diversifying, there is less chance of a total loss due to a downturn in the market. Diversification does not protect against unemployment or rising inflation rates. Although diversification may protect against international events, that is not its primary purpose.

prompt: When using the accrual method of accounting, a business pays income tax
choices: on revenues that have been invoiced, but that have not yet been received.
on expected revenues from orders that have been placed.
according to a separate set of financial records.
explanation: On revenues that have been invoiced, but that have not yet been received. The accrual method closely matches revenues and expenses to the actual period in which the transactions occur, regardless of when cash actually changes hands. Although the accrual method provides a more accurate view of the company's financials, there is also the drawback of having to pay income tax on revenues that have been invoiced, but not yet received. Expected revenues from orders that have been placed are not recognized until the product or service has been delivered, and therefore are not subject to tax. Tax is paid on cash actually received under a cash accounting method, not accrual. Income tax is paid according to the accounting method a business owner selects at the outset and not according to a separate set of financial records.

prompt: In foreign exchange markets, the major dealers are
explanation: Large banks. In foreign exchange markets, the major dealers are large banks. Businesses and countries involved in foreign exchange typically use commercial banks. These banks usually are large because they operate throughout the world. Companies not located in North America often participate in foreign exchange.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit to a business of issuing convertible bonds:
explanation: Call feature. The ability to call, or buy back, a convertible bond provides a "safety net" for companies who issue them. If interest rates decrease, a business might call the bonds in order to avoid paying high interest rates. The interest rate and maturity date are features of the convertible bond rather than benefits. The put feature is the bondholder's ability to "take back" the bond agreement.

prompt: You have incorporated your graphic design business and have been authorized to issue 100,000 shares of common stock. As a result, you are able to issue
choices: up to 100,000 shares of common or preferred stock.
up to 100,000 shares of common stock.
exactly 100,000 shares of common or preferred stock.
explanation: Up to 100,000 shares of common stock. Authorized shares do not have to be issued, but instead represent the maximum number of shares a company is legally entitled to issue. At the time of incorporation, a company specifies how much of what kind of stock it is interested in issuing-common or preferred. If preferred stock has not been authorized, it cannot be issued.

prompt: Which of the following is a factor that a growing investment business might consider when determining hiring needs:
explanation: Employee to customer ratio. Investment businesses usually consider a variety of factors when determining hiring needs because they want to hire the right number of employees. One important factor is the employee to customer ratio, particularly for businesses that interact directly with customers. For example, a business decides that it should have one employee per 10 customers. As the business estimates its rate of growth, it realizes it will need to hire additional employees to maintain the desired ratio. Qualifications of staff are considered when deciding whether to recruit internally. The type of application is not a factor. Bonuses for outstanding performance are given to employees rather than customers.

prompt: Verifying the information on a job applicant's résumé is often an important part of the __________ process.
explanation: Interview. Interviewing is an important step in the hiring process. When interviewing job applicants, interviewers often go over the information that was listed on the résumé. Many times, the interviewer wants to clarify information, such as gaps between employment or types of training. Or, the interviewer may want a more detailed explanation of what the applicant did in a previous position. Interviewers often use the résumé as the basis for obtaining additional information. During the interview, an applicant may be asked to provide additional references. Orientation occurs after an applicant has been hired. Current employees, rather than job applicants, are evaluated.

prompt: One way that businesses often use current employees during the process of orienting new employees is as
explanation: Trainers. Businesses often use current employees to help orient and train new employees. Current employees are familiar with the business's facilities and ways of operating. They can take new employees on a tour of the property, introduce them to coworkers, and explain certain basic procedures. Current employees can answer questions for new employees and help them to feel welcome in their new environment. Businesses do not use current employees to interview, manage, or evaluate new employees during the orientation process.

prompt: Is the following statement true or false: All businesses need the same types of training and human resource development.
choices: False; training/development needs vary from business to business.
True; all businesses have the same types of employees.
False; employees who transfer in do not need training.
True; all employees need some kind of classroom training.
explanation: False; training/development needs vary from business to business. Training and human resource needs vary based on the needs of the company, the specific jobs, and the individuals to be trained. Types of training should be selected based on how effectively and efficiently they will satisfy the company's operational and personnel needs. Not all businesses have the same types of employees with the same training needs. A transferred employee may still need training.

prompt: Which of the following are examples of nonfinancial rewards that businesses might give to employees:
explanation: Praise and recognition. Not all rewards are financial in nature. Some businesses reward employees by praising their accomplishments at a recognition ceremony that is attended by coworkers. The reward is the public acknowledgement. This is very motivating for some employees. However, all employees usually appreciate financial rewards, such as bonuses or gift certificates. Sweepstakes and contests are not rewards, although the end result might be a reward. For example, a contest among salespeople results in the winner receiving a reward, such as a bonus or a trip. A retirement watch has monetary value and is a reward for long-time service.

prompt: What is the overall purpose of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)?
choices: To prevent businesses from asking job applicants about their disabilities
To make it possible for qualified individuals with disabilities to get and to keep jobs
To require businesses to screen applicants with physical and/or mental disabilities
To require businesses to modify their facilities
explanation: To make it possible for qualified individuals with disabilities to get and to keep jobs. The ADA protects workers with physical and/or mental disabilities from discrimination. It does not require businesses to screen applicants with physical and/or mental disabilities. In fact, it forbids businesses from asking job applicants about current or previous disabilities and requires businesses to make their facilities accessible to those with disabilities. However, these are part of the provisions of the law, not its overall purpose.

prompt: What law affects remedial action by making discrimination in any condition of employment illegal?
choices: The Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967
The Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970
explanation: The Civil Rights Act of 1964. Businesses need to be sure that their discharge procedures are not affected by the employee's race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. The Wagner Act of 1935 covers unionized employees and stipulates that employees may not be disciplined or discharged for engaging in union activities. The Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967 covers employees between the ages of 40 and 70, forbidding their being disciplined or discharged on the basis of age. The Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970 stipulates that workers may not be disciplined or discharged for refusing to work in unsafe environments or because they report an alleged violation to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration.

prompt: The benefits that employees receive in addition to their regular wages usually increase the employees'
explanation: Total compensation. Benefits are nonmonetary payments, or indirect financial payments, that employees receive in addition to wages or salaries. These benefits often greatly increase an employee's total compensation. Types of benefits include paid vacations, participation in pension or retirement plans, and health insurance. For example, when a business pays the cost of health insurance, employees do not need to spend their own money to buy the insurance. Benefits that employees receive do not increase their value to the business, tax liability, or financial obligation.

prompt: Which of the following marketing functions is most likely to affect the image of a business:
explanation: Product/Service management. The product/service management function involves obtaining, developing, maintaining and improving a product or service mix in response to market opportunities. It affects the image of the business by creating an image for the products the business offers. Risk management is a business activity intended to limit business losses and help to assure financial security. Selling is a marketing function that involves determining client needs and wants and responding through planned, personalized communication that influences purchase decisions and enhances future business opportunities. Financing is a business function that involves understanding the financial concepts used in making business decisions.

prompt: What do managers expect tellers to do to assist with the process of auditing bank operations?
explanation: Follow standard procedures. Banks usually have standard procedures that tellers are expected to follow when an audit of the bank's operations is taking place. Audits are conducted to verify the bank's records as well as its assets and liabilities. When an audit occurs, it is usually unannounced, and tellers are expected to stop working and give the auditors access to their records and equipment. In most cases, tellers are expected to remain at their stations to answer questions, if necessary. However, they are not expected to point out problem areas because identifying errors is the job of the auditors. Audits are required in the banking industry, and banks expect tellers to cooperate fully. Tellers do not verify cash drawer amounts during an audit.

prompt: A benefit to a business that uses collaborative computer software is that it enables the employees to
explanation: Share information quickly. Collaborative computer software allows many employees to access and share the same business information. Some applications, such as e-mail, allow employees to instantly transmit messages and business documents to coworkers who are traveling or working in other facilities, which can facilitate a quick response. By sharing information quickly, employees can take immediate action and then proceed to work on other tasks. Businesses do not use collaborative computer software to enable employees to search the Web, prepare written reports, or develop keyboarding skills.

prompt: What is one of the main causes of accidents in the workplace?
explanation: Safety hazards. Safety hazards are unsafe conditions, or unsafe actions. Unsafe conditions include physical or environmental hazards in the workplace, such as poor housekeeping or fire hazards. Unsafe acts include actions that may risk safety, such as improper lifting or working when you're sleepy. These safety hazards are one of the main causes of accidents in the workplace. Physical injuries often result from accidents that occur due to safety hazards. First-aid methods are intended to provide medical assistance to injured or ill persons. Employee grievances are dissatisfactions with management, usually expressed through a formal process.

prompt: Many businesses use a variety of security precautions in order to protect the businesses from
explanation: The risk of theft. Security methods and devices protect the physical building as well as the equipment, fixtures, records, and goods stored inside. If used properly, they protect the business from the risk of theft of money and other valuables and even loss of life. Security precautions cannot protect a business from natural disasters, such as floods and lightning. Economic depressions are long periods of decline in the gross national product characterized by a period of severely lowered production, curtailed purchasing of goods and services, and high unemployment. Foreclosure is a legal procedure to sell the assets of a business that has not paid its mortgage.

prompt: Why is it important to build in a safety net, or padding, when identifying resources?
explanation: To plan for the unexpected. When identifying resources, it is important to be realistic. This often means planning for the unexpected because it's not a good idea to assume that everything will go correctly. Therefore, it is important to build in a safety net, or padding, in case something happens. For example, allow a little more time in the event that project members need to deal with other activities. It is not a good idea to try to cut corners and get by with less than you really need. Building in a safety net does not involve finding substitutes or obtaining financial support.

prompt: Comparing the prices offered by different vendors for the same goods and services is what part of the purchasing process?
explanation: Bid analysis. Businesses compare the prices offered by different vendors for the same goods and services in order to decide from whom to make the purchase. Analyzing the bids allows businesses to find out which vendor is offering the best price. Price fixing involves businesses' agreeing on prices of their products resulting in little choice for the consumer. Receipt of goods is the arrival of the order at its destination. Invoice payment is paying for the goods once they have been received.

prompt: Do businesses such as banks and dry cleaners engage in production?
choices: Yes, these businesses produce a line of tangible products.
Yes, the services provided by these businesses are their products.
No, the services provided by these businesses are intangible.
No, these businesses do not engage in production.
explanation: Yes, the services provided by these businesses are their products. Businesses are engaged in production, whether they produce goods or services. Even though services are intangible items that cannot be detected through the senses, services are products that can be sold to customers. Businesses that provide services must have a system for producing those services.

prompt: Employees who use office equipment only for company business are helping to
explanation: Control expenses. Some of a business's expenses, such as rent or insurance, cannot be controlled, but utility costs can be controlled and even reduced. Employees can help with this effort by using the telephone, fax, copier, etc., only for company business. The operating cost for this equipment increases with the amount of use; therefore, using it only for company business will help to control expenses. Using office equipment only for company business does not help to reduce waste, identify theft, or spend revenues.

prompt: A business leases 2,225 square feet of space at $2.30 per square foot per month. If the rent will increase by 3% next year, calculate the yearly amount the business will pay in rent.
explanation: $63,252.30. The rent for space often increases every year unless the business negotiates a long-term lease for a specific price. In this example, the rent will increase by 3%. To calculate the increase, first determine the current monthly rent by multiplying the square feet by the rental rate (2,225 x $2.30 = $5,117.50). Then, multiply that amount by 12 to determine the current yearly rent ($5,117.50 x 12 = $61,410). Finally, multiply the current rent by the 3% increase to determine the amount of increase and add the increase to the current rent to determine next year's rent ($61,410 x 3% or .03 = $1,842.30; $61,410.00 + $1,842.30 = $63,252.30).

prompt: A business's budget estimated $165,500 in sales each month for the next four months with 55% of that amount each month for expenses. If actual sales for the four-month period were $690,000 and expenses stayed at 55%, by what amount did the business's income increase?
explanation: $12,600. Businesses use budget information to monitor sales and expenses and to compare budgeted amounts with actual figures. If sales increase over the amount budgeted and expenses remain steady, the business's income will also increase. In this example, the business's actual sales increased over the budgeted amount. To calculate the increase in income, first determine the budgeted four-month sales total ($165,500 x 4 = $662,000). Then, calculate the amount of that figure that was budgeted for expenses ($662,000 x 55% or .55 = $364,100). Then, subtract budgeted expenses from budgeted sales to calculate budgeted income ($662,000 - $364,100 = $297,900). Next, calculate the amount of expenses based on actual sales ($690,000 x 55% or .55 = $379,500). Subtract expenses from actual sales to calculate actual income ($690,000 - $379,500 = $310,500). To determine the increase in income, subtract budgeted income from actual income ($310,500 - $297,900 = $12,600).

prompt: Businesses that offer flextime usually schedule all employees to work during __________ time.
explanation: Core. Businesses that offer flextime usually require all employees to work during core time, which is a specific block of time generally ranging from mid-morning to mid-afternoon. Businesses schedule all employees to be on hand during core time because it usually is the busiest time of the day. Employees then may schedule the remainder of their work day around the core hours. Some employees may choose to come in early and leave when core time ends, or come in when core time begins and leave later in the day. Sale time is when the price of goods and services is reduced. Peak refers to the highest level or greatest degree, such as reaching the high point of development. Lead time is the amount of time that passes between placing an order and receiving the stock.

prompt: Which of the following would be most helpful in achieving a financial goal that involves a major purchase:
choices: Looking for ways to save money
Comparing the quality of various brands
explanation: Looking for ways to save money. Making a major purchase, such as a car or a house, means spending a considerable sum of money. This kind of financial goal can be reached more quickly if the individual looks for ways in which s/he can save money to be used toward the purchase. Comparing the quality of brands will help determine the amount of money needed but will not help to reach the purchase goal. Discussing the goal with friends would also not help, and establishing a short time limit might make the goal impossible to reach.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of creativity:
choices: Suggesting a new way to organize stock
Turning in a $20 bill a customer left on the counter
explanation: Suggesting a new way to organize stock. Creativity is the ability to generate unique ideas, approaches, and solutions. Turning in a $20 bill is being honest. Greeting customers by name shows interest in customers. Reporting for work on time is acting responsibly.

prompt: Which of the following is a source of career information that is easy to contact:
explanation: Relatives. Relatives are often a good source of career information, and they are also easy to contact. Family members may work in various types of professions or industries and be able to explain the job requirements and advancement opportunities. They may be able to provide brochures or reports from their places of employment that describe the jobs and the purpose of the business. Family members are usually willing to talk about their jobs and provide information to young relatives. Although it is possible to obtain career information from employers, research institutions, and government agencies, it is not always easy to do so. Some of these organizations do not have easily-accessible information or have restrictions on who may receive the information.

prompt: Is it ever appropriate for an individual looking for a job to send a letter of application to a business that has not advertised a job opening?
choices: Yes, the worker can write if s/he has heard about a job opening.
Yes, the worker should write to each business in the industry.
No, the business will discard the letter if it has no openings.
No, a letter is used only in response to job advertisements.
explanation: Yes, the worker can write if s/he has heard about a job opening. In some cases, a worker looking for a job will hear about a job opening from some other source than a job advertisement. It is acceptable for the worker to write a letter stating that s/he has heard of an opening and asking to be considered for the position. In some cases, this results in an interview and a job. Most companies do not discard such letters but keep them on file in case of future need. It would not be appropriate or practical to send letters to all businesses in the industry.

prompt: Which of the following is a characteristic of employees who are often promoted and given supervisory responsibilities:
explanation: Productive. Productivity is the amount of work employees perform in a given period, usually their output per hour. Employees who are productive and perform well on the job are often recognized for their efforts and promoted. Productive employees frequently are given supervisory responsibilities because their performance indicates that they are capable of accomplishing the goals of the business. Employees who are aggressive often ignore the rights of others and take advantage of them to achieve personal goals. Employees who are defensive have negative attitudes toward criticism or suggestions. Employees who are submissive are compliant and do not voice their own opinions.

prompt: In most businesses, the treasurer is not responsible for which of the following:
explanation: Managing the accounting department. In most businesses, the treasurer is responsible for managing the firm's cash, planning the firm's capital structure, and managing risk-in addition to other responsibilities. The controller is typically responsible for the activities of the accounting department. Oversight of the treasurer and controller is the responsibility of the chief financial officer (or vice president of finance).

prompt: In selling, effective salespeople use the art of good questioning in order to determine the customer's
explanation: Needs, wants, and buying motives. A salesperson's questions must show a concern for the customer, since a purpose of selling is to assist the customer in making a wise buying decision. The remaining alternatives are not appropriate subjects for questioning.

prompt: An investment business's ultimate goal is to sell products in order to stay in business. Therefore, the substitute product that a salesperson recommends should always
explanation: Satisfy the client's needs. Only by satisfying the client's real needs can an investment business continue to operate. The quality, price, and benefits to the client of substitute products should all be in keeping with the client's original request in order to meet the customer's needs.

prompt: At what point in the selling process is it best to close the sale?
choices: After the presentation of the product
explanation: Anytime during the presentation. The sales close may come at any time. The close really begins when the salesperson starts the sales presentation. It may occur as early as the approach, at any point during the sales presentation, while overcoming objections, or when discussing terms of payment. Salespeople must always be alert for the opportunity to close.

prompt: When a financial client pays you with a traveler's check, you should
choices: require the check to be certified.
encourage the client to use a personal check.
watch the client countersign the check.
ask the client to show you identification.
explanation: Watch the client countersign the check. When a financial client pays you with a traveler's check, it is important to watch the client countersign the check and compare that signature with the one in the upper left-hand corner. If the two signatures match, you can accept the check as valid. Since you are using a signature to determine authenticity, you do not need to see the client's identification. The traveler's check does not need to be certified, and the client does not need to be encouraged to use another form of payment, such as a personal check.

prompt: A check presented for payment is presumed to be "stale-dated" when the date on which it is presented is
choices: the day after it is drawn.
after 4:00 p.m. on the day it is drawn.
more than 30 days from the date it is drawn.
explanation: More than 30 days from the date it is drawn. A check is normally considered stale when it is presented for payment more than 30 days from the date on which it was drawn. After six months, the paying financial institution has no obligation to pay a routine check. A check is not presumed to be stale when presented "the day after it is drawn," "10 days after the date shown," and "after 4:00 p.m. on the day it is drawn."

prompt: Susan has a middle management position in her company. Her primary job responsibility is likely to be
choices: establishing the weekly work schedules for employees.
developing the plans and goals for the company.
spending one day a week on each management function.
being responsible for other managers or supervisors.
explanation: Being responsible for other managers or supervisors. Mid-level, or middle, managers report to top-level management and have supervisors who report to them. Plans and goals for the company are developed by top management. Susan is likely to be involved in some aspect(s) of more than one management function at any one time. Establishing weekly work schedules is a task of supervisory, or first-level, managers who work directly with the employees who carry out the business's routine work.

prompt: Ethical managers have the ability to make impartial judgments about employees and their actions without
explanation: Showing favoritism. Ethics are the basic principles that govern a person's behavior. A manager who shows impartiality and has the ability to make judgments without showing favoritism or demonstrating self-interest is exhibiting fair and ethical behavior. In other words, the manager is able to use the same criteria to judge all employees rather than give special consideration to a few. Being emotional, feeling inferior, and expressing criticism usually do not impact the ability to behave ethically.

prompt: In which of the following situations will a business plan that includes monthly sales goals help a company to track its progress and make adjustments:
choices: Each salesperson has a monthly sales quota.
Monthly sales are the same as last month.
Sales figures decrease 10% in the summer.
explanation: Actual sales are 75% of estimate. One of the purposes of developing a business plan that includes monthly sales goals is to provide the company with a tool for tracking its progress. An effective business plan includes a way to measure performance on a regular basis rather than waiting until the end of the year to find out if the goals have been met. Many plans contain monthly sales goals which can be compared to actual sales to determine if the business is on track or needs to make adjustments. If actual sales are only 75% of the monthly goal, the business will want to make changes to improve its performance. A business plan might set the same sales goals for several consecutive months. Business plans usually take into consideration seasonal fluctuations in sales. Each salesperson might have a monthly sales quota, which usually is set by the sales manager based on the goals outlined in the business plan.
